title: Not allegorizing the bad, guarding speech and temper
english: Do not allegorize the words of blameworthy people, and do not look for anything spiritual in them, unless God through divine arrangement has worked in them, as with Balaam and Caiaphas, so that the one foretold our Savior's birth and the other foretold His death.

The gnostic must be neither gloomy nor hard to approach. Gloom belongs to one who does not know the principles of the things that come to be, and being hard to approach belongs to one who does not want all people to be saved and to come to recognition of the truth (1 Timothy 2:4).

Watch yourself, lest for the sake of gain or comfort, or for the sake of passing glory, you speak anything of the secret teachings and are cast outside the sacred enclosures, like a man selling the young of doves in the temple.
Do not speak about God recklessly, and never define the divine. Definitions belong to things that have been made and put together.
[Part of the text is missing.] The one who has been tried by evil hates evil, and trial is the child of abandonment. [Part of the text is missing.]
Let those you teach always say to you, "Friend, come up higher" (Luke 14:10). For it is shameful, after you have gone up, to be pulled down again by your hearers.
The lover of money is not the one who has money, but the one who longs for it. For they say the steward is a reasoning purse.
Urge older men to master anger and younger men to master the belly. For demons that war against the soul assail the former, while demons that war against the body for the most part assail the latter.

Shut the mouths of those who speak ill of others within your hearing, and do not be surprised when many accuse you. That trial comes from demons. For the gnostic must be free from hatred and from holding memory of injury, even when others do not wish it.
The one who heals people for the sake of the Lord may heal himself without noticing it. For the remedy the gnostic offers heals his neighbor possibly, but heals himself necessarily.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Evagrius continues his counsels to the gnostic on when not to speak of divine things and how to remain free from anger and accusation.

title: Guarding the higher word and the gnostic's trials
english: Keep the higher word about judgment hidden from worldly people and the young, since it easily produces contempt. They do not know the pain of a rational soul condemned to ignorance.
Saint Paul, by buffeting, enslaved the body (1 Corinthians 9:27). So do not neglect the diet in your life, and do not insult freedom from passion by humbling it with a fat body.
Do not worry about food or clothing, but remember Abinadab the Levite, who received the ark of the Lord and from poverty became rich, and from dishonor became honored (1 Samuel 7:1).

Every proposition has either a genus as predicate, or a difference, or a species, or a property, or an accident, or something composed of these. But none of these can be grasped in the case of the Holy Trinity. In silence let the ineffable be worshipped.
The temptation of a gnostic is a false supposition that occurs in the mind: that what exists does not exist, that what does not exist does exist, and that what exists is not as it actually is.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Evagrius is giving counsels to the gnostic about guarding higher teaching, bodily discipline, freedom from care, the ineffable Trinity, and the nature of the gnostic's temptation.

title: The four virtues and the teachers of the gnostic
english: We have learned from the just Gregory that contemplation itself has four virtues: prudence, courage, temperance, and justice. He used to say that the work of prudence is to contemplate the intelligent and holy powers without the principles, for he taught that these are made known only by wisdom. The work of courage, he said, is to stand firm in the truths even when attacked, and not to intrude into the things that are not. He declared that the special mark of temperance is to receive the seeds from the first farmer and to reject the one who sows afterward. And the work of justice, again, is to give to each the principles according to worth, declaring some things darkly, signifying others through riddles, and revealing still others for the benefit of the simpler ones.

Basil the Cappadocian, the pillar of truth, says that the spiritual knowledge that comes from human beings is strengthened by constant study and practice, but the spiritual knowledge that arises in us from God's grace is strengthened by justice, freedom from anger, and mercy. The former, he says, can be received even by those still subject to passion, but only those free from passion are capable of receiving the latter. These are the ones who, at the time of prayer, behold the proper radiance of the mind shining around them.

The holy luminary of the Egyptians, Athanasius, says that Moses is commanded to set the table on the north side (Exodus 26:35). Let the gnostics know who it is that blows against them, and let them endure every temptation nobly, and let them feed those who come to them with eagerness.

The angel of the church of the Thmuites, Sarapion, used to say that the mind that has drunk spiritual knowledge is completely purified, that love heals the inflamed parts of the irascible faculty, and that self-control stops the evil desires that flow in.

The great and gnostic teacher Didymus says: Always train by yourself the discourses on providence and judgment, and try to carry their subject matter in your memory, for nearly everyone stumbles in these matters. You will find the discourses on judgment in the difference of bodies and worlds, and the discourses on providence in the ways that lead us back from vice and ignorance to virtue or to spiritual knowledge.
Always looking to the original pattern, try to write the images, omitting nothing that helps to recover what has fallen.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Evagrius is closing his treatise by recalling what he learned from approved teachers about the virtues, knowledge, and the training of the mind.
